steps.description: We begin with the helper that every other module leans on – `FixedPointMath`.  It stores decimal numbers with 18-decimals of precision and exposes arithmetic helpers that automatically keep that scale.
DECIMALS is hard-coded to 18 and ONE = 10 ** 18 – this single constant encodes the value 1.0 in the chosen fixed-point representation.
Every fixed-point value is wrapped in the lightweight struct Number which contains one field – n – the raw scaled uint256.
encodeRaw(value) multiplies an integer by ONE, returning the raw scaled uint256; encode(value) simply wraps that result in Number.
Utility constructors: max() returns the biggest possible scaled value; rational(n,d) builds n / d by encoding the numerator and then dividing by the denominator.
add overloads: Number + Number simply adds their raw fields; Number + uint256 transparently encodes the integer before adding – callers do not need to scale literals themselves.
sub follows the same pattern – direct subtraction for Number vs. Number and automatic encoding when the right-hand operand is a plain integer.
mul/div: When both operands are Numbers the product is divided by ONE to re-normalise the scale (line 116).  Multiplying by an integer or dividing by an integer needs no rescale.
cmp returns −1 / 0 / 1 depending on ordering, mirroring the behaviour of many standard libraries; equals is the shorter boolean check.
`truncate` removes the fractional component by dividing by `ONE`, yielding the integer part of the fixed-point number.
Casting between signed and unsigned values is concentrated in `SafeCast` – every **narrowing conversion** reverts instead of silently wrapping.
`toInt256(uint256)` reverts when the input would overflow `int256`; `toUint256(int256)` reverts on negative values – both guard against undefined behaviour.
`uint256ToUint128` enforces the down-cast is in range; `uint128ToUint256` is a safe, trivial up-cast.
With these two helpers in mind you can now recognise every place in the codebase where **precise decimal math** or **safe integer casting** is performed.
